title: Off-Policy vs On-Policy Activations Break Deception Probes

original_idea.body:
# Off-Policy vs On-Policy Activations Break Deception Probes

**Problem:** Deception probes trained on off-policy (forced) data hurt performance vs on-policy; the gap is under-measured on open models.

**Direction:** On an open instruction model, build two deception probe training sets (forced vs model-generated) and measure cross-transfer.

**Why it matters:** Probes relying on elicitation artifacts fail on genuine behavior. No lab resources.

**Relevant context:** OpenReview IOR5bkd0ep; arXiv 2502.03407.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: deception-monitor reliability is a recognized critical pathway; on/off-policy gap directly affects deployment trust.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Train two linear probes and measure transfer on one open model; guided and tractable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single transfer measurement with clear gap metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Diffuse evaluation work, open model, lab-deprioritized; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation extraction + linear probes on an open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The off/on-policy effect is flagged in recent work; quantifying it on open models may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The effect is reported; open-model quantification of the gap may be open.
